question: Can a single sentence measure its candidate-specific nuisance advantage by interchanging two physical nominees' learned decoder slot positions?
intervention: Keep the sentence, sampled scene, reference slots and native priors fixed to their physical boxes. Swap only the positions of two subject boxes together with their priors in the decoder input, then undo the permutation on the output. Evaluate all six swaps and the native order in one decoder batch. For each oriented physical pair compute half the difference between its native and swapped margin.
measured_target: On a shared slate for two same-frame naturally opposed captions, the average of their same-orientation frozen margins is the common preference. Train on two-sentence source nominations from 213 potential Waymo TRAIN pairs. Learn the signed mean per unordered pair of slot positions. Within each rank pair, regress measured common preference on centered swap response with one shared coefficient. Uniform averaging over the pair's two orderings, the original v1 and the fitted rank-only mean are controls. Physical instance comparisons remain in the shared coordinates.
decoder: For four-way inference subtract the complete-graph least-squares potential, row sums of the antisymmetric bias estimates divided by four. Keep pairwise correction diagnostics distinct from actual four-way output. All seven reads see the very same input and no new backbone features.
decision: Only consider target expansion if the state-specific intervention reduces held-out nuisance MSE beyond rank-only AND yields more doubly correct source pairs than rank-only without losing four-way doubly correct cases on the recording-confirmation panel. Existing 44 natural development pairs and 142 pairs in 80 recordings are reused here and disclosed. A failure ends this slot-intervention recipe. All missed endpoints retained. No FINAL, target labels, or backbone optimization.
